UHON 351

AI Safety and Society

  • Undergraduate honors
  • 3 credits

Offered: Spring 2026

This honors seminar examines AI safety as a societal and ethical challenge. Students explore how AI risks arise, who is affected, and how governance can protect individuals and communities while supporting beneficial uses.

Selected Topics

  • Machine learning and large language model fundamentals
  • Societal and catastrophic risks from advanced AI
  • Transparency, robustness, and unintended behavior
  • Machine ethics, collective action, and international governance

Learning Objectives

  • Identify and explain major ethical and societal AI risks.
  • Use ethical frameworks to evaluate competing values and decisions.
  • Develop practical governance proposals that address AI safety challenges.

Coursework & Projects

Team case studies, discussions, reflective essays, and quizzes build understanding. Collaborative projects develop policy proposals or ethical frameworks for managing AI risks.
